title: The research shelf
intro: The full case — every citation behind our belief that transparency and direct participation, tied into the republic we already have, are the future of American self-government. Organized by claim. Where the evidence is mixed, we say so; a shelf that hides its weak spots is marketing.

themes.claim: 1 · The republic was built with room for this
themes.summary: Direct local participation is not a departure from the American design — it predates the Constitution and runs beside it. New England towns have governed by open assembly since the 1630s; the Constitution guarantees every state a republican form while towns kept their meetings; Tocqueville called town institutions the schools where liberty is learned. Signal-not-command platforms extend this lineage without touching anyone's constitutional authority.

themes.claim: 2 · The trust crisis is real and measured
themes.summary: Three-quarters of Americans say trust in the federal government is shrinking; two generations of civic-connection decline are documented in everything from meeting attendance to league bowling. This is the diagnosis that makes participation infrastructure a treatment, not a hobby.

citations.label: Pew Research — Americans' declining trust in government and each other (2019)

themes.claim: 3 · Transparency works — when it comes with a way to act (the honest mixed evidence)
themes.summary: The research record on transparency alone is mixed: open budgeting and clear communication measurably raise trust in some studies, while in others, disclosure without responsiveness breeds resignation — citizens see the problems and withdraw. The literature's convergent lesson is the one this platform is built on: transparency plus voice plus a visible response loop, never transparency as a spectator sport.

themes.summary: A single structured deliberation produced measurable knowledge gains and large effects on civic engagement and voting nearly a year later. Participatory budgeting made participants more politically active and raised turnout among groups that usually stay home. The deepest return on being asked is what it does to the person asked.

themes.claim: 5 · Communities agree on more than their arguments suggest
themes.summary: Taiwan's no-replies statement voting repeatedly found silent majorities under loud fights and produced real regulation; the mechanics — no threads, bridge statements scored across groups — are inheritable by any county.

citations.label: vTaiwan — Participedia case study
Polis — the clustering method

themes.claim: 6 · It runs at government scale, today, in forms officials embrace
themes.summary: Switzerland votes ~15 times a year and its direct forms work best at small scale; Reykjavik reached more than half its city with a monthly council-review commitment; Madrid put 400,000 registered residents' top proposals into the draft budget; Barcelona's open-source kernel now runs hundreds of instances; the UK's petition thresholds guarantee a government response at 10,000 signatures; a Wisconsin county reallocated 15% of its budget by making priorities visible; Vermont's Front Porch Forum leaves 81% of members feeling more informed (vs. 26% on Facebook).

themes.claim: 7 · The failure modes are known — and designable-around
themes.summary: California shows what binding, money-soaked, high-volume direct democracy can break; Porto Alegre shows what champion-dependence costs; the research also finds the popular fears (incompetent voters, captured masses) largely overstated. Every failure mode maps to a design answer: non-binding signal, no signature industry, few questions with context, bright lines, durable cheap infrastructure.

themes.claim: 8 · Self-governance of shared resources is a science with a Nobel Prize
themes.summary: Ostrom's field research established that communities can govern commons durably when the governed help make the rules, monitoring is community-answerable, and conflict resolution is cheap — design principles this platform implements for the commons called a county budget.

citations.label: Ostrom — Governing the Commons (Cambridge)
Beyond Intractability — Governing the Commons summary

closing: Twenty-nine citations, eight claims, one design: the republic keeps its officials and its elections; residents gain sight of the money, a voice between ballots, and a count nobody has to take on faith. Deeper treatments of each precedent live in the evidence library, and the platform that implements all of it is the site you are standing in.
